_README: Provenance for every fixture. Read this before trusting one. 'observed' means these are real records an API returned on the recorded date, and may be cited. 'unverified' means the shape was written from documentation and has never been seen from the live API - it is safe to test against, but must NOT be cited as evidence of what the API returns.
_anonymisation: Every observed fixture has been through processing.anonymise: name, pseudonym, bio and profileImage removed; proxyWallet replaced with a stable hash. Per the ethics protocol no identifying profile data is committed. tests/test_fixtures.py re-checks this on every run.
_refreshing: python tests/record_fixtures.py --help. Needs a normal network connection. Re-record only when the API changes shape, and say so in the commit message - a test that silently starts passing against different data is worse than one that fails.

trades.json.notes: Unscoped /trades call against the live global feed. Short-dated BTC up/down markets, which is what that feed is mostly made of.

trades_maduro.json.notes: Seed-case market (Maduro), takerOnly=false. TRUNCATED to 25 rows, so it is not a full 500-row page - do not use it to test end-of-page detection.

activity.json.notes: Types present: REDEEM, TRADE. No DEPOSIT or WITHDRAWAL rows: this recording did not target a wallet with funding events, so it cannot exercise the wallet-funding features. Record one that does before WS7.

closed_positions.json.notes: Carries realizedPnl and avgPrice - the two fields every profitability feature depends on.

positions.json.notes: The data dictionary marks no /positions field as (obs) - this endpoint has never been called. Fields here are the documented ones plus proxyWallet and asset by analogy with the other endpoints. The real response probably carries more. Replace this with a real recording on the next live run.

error_429.json.notes: Polymarket's actual 429 body has not been captured. The body text is a guess; the status code is what the tests care about.

gamma_markets.json.source: hand-built from docs/data_dictionary.md field list + config/seeds.json
gamma_markets.json.notes: SHAPE ONLY - never cite this as evidence of what Gamma returns. The conditionId, question and date values are real: they are the three seed markets and the two control markets from config/seeds.json. Slugs for the two control markets were derived from their titles, because seeds.json does not record them. Every other value is synthetic. The five records deliberately vary in shape to exercise the coercion branches: string vs numeric liquidityNum/volumeNum, JSON-encoded vs real-list outcomes and clobTokenIds, tags on the market vs only on its parent event, eventSlug given directly vs via events[], a null createdAt, and liquidity/volume under the un-suffixed key names. Replace with a live recording: python tests/record_fixtures.py --endpoint /markets.

gamma_events.json.source: hand-built from docs/data_dictionary.md field list + config/seeds.json
gamma_events.json.notes: SHAPE ONLY - never cite this as evidence of what Gamma returns. Parent events for the markets in gamma_markets.json, so the markets[].conditionId join can be tested. The Harris market in event 903 is invented, including its conditionId - it is there to give one event more than a single market. Event 5388 carries bare-string tags rather than tag objects, to exercise that branch of extract_tags(). Replace with a live recording: python tests/record_fixtures.py --endpoint /events.
